correctness.rationale: Use unnormalized Haar+tau delta_0. Orthogonality of Phi_m(z)=z^m−a∑_{j=0}^{m−1}z^j, a=tau/(1+m tau), is exact because the Haar constant coefficient cancels the atom evaluation for each low Fourier test. Its symmetric paraorthogonal polynomial B_m has real boundary expression e^(-imt/2)B_m(e^{it})=cos(mt/2)−a cot(t/2)sin(mt/2). The ratio tan(mt/2)/tan(t/2) rises strictly from m to infinity on (0,pi/m), so the nearest zero is unique; Ismoilov (2026) Theorem 1 supplies sharp sign radius, zero mean and extremizer uniqueness in the general symmetric measure problem, credited as prior. x=m t solves tan(x/2)/(m tan(x/(2m)))=1+1/(m tau). Uniform compact convergence and monotone inversion yield m tau→c, c→0 and c→infinity regimes; R_m(x)=1+(1−m^-2)x²/12+O(x^4) gives rho m^(3/2) sqrt(tau)→sqrt(3)/pi in the large regime. Rescaling the self-reciprocal polynomial h and cosine difference gives profile 2G_c(u)^2/(u²−x_c²), with moving removable poles handled by local holomorphic factorization, including coalescing c=infinity roots. Independent 1196 exact rational Gram equations and 12 critical-root comparisons corroborate. Note m>=2 and tau>=0 boundaries explicitly.
